title: Ukraine Pivots to Israeli-Italian Satellite Tech to Bypass Starlink Restrictions
excerpt: Ukrainian drone units adopt HiSky satellite terminals to maintain deep-strike capabilities after Starlink disruptions threatened critical military comms.
content_html:
POLICY WIRE — Kyiv, Ukraine — The Ukrainian Armed Forces are actively diversifying their communications infrastructure to reduce a strategic dependence on Elon Musk’s Starlink service. This shift follows reports that restrictions on the military-grade Starshield network recently forced the cancellation of vital drone missions.

Russian military channels claimed on November 6 that Ukrainian units have begun utilizing specialized satellite terminals from the Israeli manufacturer HiSKY for their deep-strike operations. These 6-kilogram devices are seen as a functional alternative to the SpaceX-operated network previously dominated battlefield connectivity.

Russian engineers have been investigating the high precision and success of recent Ukrainian drone attacks on domestic oil refineries. The discovery of HiSky technology may provide answers regarding how Ukraine has maintained operational effectiveness despite fluctuations in its primary satellite access.

The move toward rival providers highlights the vulnerability exposed when a military relies on a single commercial entity for critical infrastructure. Recently, Ukrainian units experienced dropped connections and diminished operational speeds when Starshield services were suddenly restricted, causing significant tactical setbacks.

Competing satellite firms are now seeking to fill the void left by SpaceX’s perceived unpredictability on the battlefield. By integrating Israeli and Italian-developed technology, Kyiv aims to ensure that its strike capabilities are not subject to the corporate or political decisions of a single provider.
